clue.text: A hundred animals devouring odd items of food

indicators.note: the outer pieces eat up, so enclose, the word for odd

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
pets are animals kept at home
rum is an old-fashioned word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A hundred creatures tucking into strange bits of food.
explanation.walkthrough: A crumpet is a soft, holey griddle cake toasted and buttered for tea in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Crumpets are griddle cakes, a typical British teatime food served toasted with butter.

clue.text: Spice plant makin' progress, from what we hear

indicators.note: the phrase signals that the letters entered match a word as spoken

parts.note: coming along, clipped to comin' to match the dropped g of makin'

explanation.surface: A plant that is coming on nicely, said in a casual accent.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped g in makin' hints that the word said aloud is also clipped: comin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cummin is an old spelling of cumin, the plant whose seeds are a common spice.

clue.text: International organisation suffers things best hidden in polite society?

definitions.text: things best hidden in polite society?

parts.note: UN is the United Nations
to die can mean to suffer greatly, as in dying of embarrassment

explanation.surface: A global body endures things that ought to stay out of polite conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwear is kept out of sight in company, a playful circumlocution for knickers and pants.

clue.text: Out-of-date academic died

parts.note: passé means old-fashioned or out of date
a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: An outmoded scholar has passed away.
explanation.definitionFit: Passed on is a gentle euphemism for having died.

clue.text: Give away secrets in hotel lounge

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of the two words hotel lounge

explanation.surface: Spilling confidential information in a hotel bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell on someone is to reveal what they wanted kept private; blab is a synonym.

clue.text: Friend trapped in Asian country — where this was used destructively

indicators.note: one piece is caught inside the other

parts.note: Nam is the short informal name for Vietnam
pal is an informal word for a friend

explanation.surface: A friend stuck in Vietnam, where a terrible weapon was deployed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wordplay: Nam (Vietnam) is the country where the incendiary was used, so the clue defines the answer by its history.
explanation.definitionFit: Napalm, jellied incendiary fuel, was notoriously dropped by US forces during the Vietnam War.

clue.text: Good-looker's mission that was out of this world

definitions.meaning: a very handsome man may be called an Adonis or a god of beauty, after the Greek deity of light and music

definitions.text: mission that was out of this world
definitions.meaning: the American programme of crewed Moon flights, literally beyond the Earth

explanation.surface: A handsome man whose task was simply fabulous.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god was an ideal of male beauty, and the NASA Moon programme bore his name.

clue.text: Twit belonging to the upper classes matured and softened

parts.note: an ass is a fool or twit
U stands for upper-class usage, as in U and non-U
aged means grown old or matured, as with cheese or wine

explanation.surface: A posh fool who grew older and mellowed.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U were labels popularised in 1950s Britain for upper-class versus middle-class speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To assuage is to ease or relieve, so assuaged pain has been softened.

clue.text: Be more laid back, stupid!

definitions.meaning: to care less about something, read as two words

explanation.surface: Someone told to relax and called an idiot in the same breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Mindless means senseless or brainless, and minding less means worrying less.

clue.text: Member of teenage group changing style with diffidence

parts.note: a mod belonged to the 1960s British youth subculture of scooters and sharp suits

indicators.note: the letters of style are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A 1960s youngster quietly altering his look.
explanation.walkthrough: Mods were a 1960s British youth movement known for scooters and tailored suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Modestly means humbly, without pushing oneself forward, which is diffidence in manner.

clue.text: Relation needing a bit of money to cross America

indicators.note: the coin stretches over and around the other piece

parts.note: a coin is a single piece of money
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A relative short of cash wanting to travel across America.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is a family member, a child of one's aunt or uncle.

clue.text: The group of us facing a defeat get utterly tired

parts.note: we is the pronoun for a group including the speaker
taken as written
a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: Our team, facing a thrashing, becomes completely exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear out is to become exhausted, used up or fatigued through effort.

clue.text: One insect's nipped ten goats

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the insects grip the ten between them, holding it inside

parts.note: bees, read as plural rather than possessive
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A single insect has bitten ten goats.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in insect's is ignored: read it as BEES, plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibexes are wild mountain goats of the Alps and other ranges, with long curved horns.

clue.text: Rebuke sounded in Midlands university's accommodation

indicators.note: the letters entered match a phrase as it is spoken

parts.note: a hall of residence at Keele University in Staffordshire, in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: A telling-off heard in a student residence in the Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: Keele is a university town in Staffordshire; Keele hall sounds like the old naval punishment of dragging under a ship's hull.
explanation.definitionFit: Keelhauling was a naval punishment, so the word figuratively means to scold severely.

clue.text: The woman secluded by trees made a sibilant sound

indicators.note: the trees hide the woman away inside them

parts.note: woods are areas of trees
she is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman hidden among the trees made a hissing noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A whoosh is a rushing, hissing noise, so this past tense means hissed or swished.

clue.text: Thus little woman needs vessel for short stay

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
Jo March is one of the sisters in Little Women
an urn is a vessel or vase

explanation.surface: So a petite lady needs a container for a brief visit.
explanation.walkthrough: Little woman points to Jo, the heroine of Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: A sojourn is a temporary stay somewhere, a short visit.

clue.text: God gets place of the Egyptians overthrown

indicators.note: turned over, so the place name is read backwards in an across light

parts.note: Suez is a port city and canal in Egypt

explanation.surface: A deity takes an Egyptian spot that has been toppled.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus was king of the Greek gods, ruling from Mount Olympus.

clue.text: Alarm should be loud? Correct!

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical direction for loud
to righten is to set right or correct

explanation.surface: Ought the warning to be noisy? Yes, quite right!
explanation.definitionFit: To frighten is to scare or startle someone, filling them with alarm.

clue.text: One gets upset during awful frost — was it this?

indicators.note: one piece goes within the other
the letters of frost are messed up into a different order
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards or on dice

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles in a hard frost; was it predicted?
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' looks like a pronoun but is the card ace. The clue as a whole asks whether a weather prediction foresaw the frost.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather prediction might have warned of the frost described, hence the question.

clue.text: Town employees north of ring road

indicators.note: in a down light the first piece sits above, so before, the rest

parts.note: staff are the people employed by a firm
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: Workers based north of the ring road in a town.
explanation.definitionFit: Stafford is the county town of Staffordshire in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Cheat and criminal getting caught out — put in bird

indicators.note: the abbreviation for caught is left out of the word

parts.note: a crook is a criminal
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A swindler and a lawbreaker exposed and sent down, while a bird looks on.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also a bird of the crow family, which the clue tacks on at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is to swindle or defraud them.

clue.text: When to resign? Hard for a PM

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
to quit is to resign or leave a post
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Asking when a prime minister should step down when things get tough.
explanation.walkthrough: H.H. Asquith was the Liberal Prime Minister of Britain from 1908 to 1916.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert Asquith led the British government as Prime Minister before and during part of WWI.

clue.text: One part of plant or a second lacking oxygen

indicators.note: without, so the chemical symbol is removed

parts.note: another means one more, a second of the same
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A piece of a plant, or a second one missing its oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: The anther is the pollen-bearing tip of a flower's stamen.

clue.text: Pussy clawing very little men in frolic

indicators.note: the cat holds the others in its claws, enclosing them

parts.note: a pussy is a cat
V is the abbreviation for very, a little form of the word
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A cat scratching tiny men at play.
explanation.definitionFit: To cavort is to leap or prance about excitedly, to frolic.

clue.text: Becoming wily when penning English, this writer flipped

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so the outer word holds the rest

parts.note: sly means cunning or wily

indicators.note: in a down light flipped means turned over, read backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A crafty person writing about English becomes a flipped writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Becoming is the adjective meaning suitable, not the verb, and 'this writer' is the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemly means fitting or proper, as becoming does when describing behaviour.

clue.text: Island that could give us energy supply

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, meaning flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: An island that might provide us with power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is read as the adverb from supple, flexibly, rearranging US ENERGY. Guernsey is one of the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Guernsey is the second-largest of the Channel Islands, between England and France.

clue.text: One losing heart, dejected inside, recently

indicators.note: the second piece goes within the first
the middle letter of the word one is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before the middle letter goes
flat means dull or low in spirits

explanation.surface: Someone discouraged, feeling low within, in recent times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' leaves the outer letters O and E of the numeral word, which then hold the low-spirited word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Of late is an idiom meaning lately or in recent times.

clue.text: A jewel has turned up — it's enormous

indicators.note: in a down light turned up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a gem is a jewel

explanation.surface: A precious stone appears, and it is huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is a slang adjective meaning huge or tremendous.

clue.text: Awful crack gathering dust

indicators.note: the outer word collects the other inside it

parts.note: a crack is an attempt, a try
ash is the dusty residue of burning

explanation.surface: A dreadful fissure collecting grime.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashy means of poor quality, rubbishy, so awful in the casual sense.

clue.text: Bottle tramp wrapped in lots of paper

indicators.note: the vagrant is enclosed by the paper

parts.note: a ream is 500 sheets of paper
a hobo is a tramp or vagrant

explanation.surface: Bottle of booze for a vagrant swaddled in newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehoboam is a large wine or champagne bottle holding six standard bottles.

clue.text: The countryside turning brown by northern river

indicators.note: turning round, so the colour word is read backwards

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Fields turning brown beside a river in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Nature is the natural world of plants, animals and landscape, the countryside.

clue.text: Gang — it may go by rail for criminal activity

parts.note: a band is a group or gang
taken as written
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A gang may travel by train for a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Banditry is robbery by bandits, lawless plunder and violence.
